item.title: EU releases €1.24 billion for Ukrainian-made drones and munitions
item.description: The European Union has released €1.24 billion for Ukraine to buy drones, drone interceptors, drone ammunition and munitions manufactured domestically in a bid to push back against Russia's ongoing and escalated air attacks.

item.title: Plague fears in Siberia: How are Irkutsk residents reacting?
item.description: Irkutsk residents react to reports of a suspected pneumonic plague death at a local anti-plague institute, with authorities saying the cause of death remains unconfirmed.

item.title: Kyiv residents take refuge underground during overnight Russian attacks
item.description: Kyiv residents took refuge in metro stations, preparing to sleep underground before a Russian missile and drone attack killed at least eight people.

item.title: French and Japanese scientists win 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for what could change how medicines are made
item.description: Two researchers have won this year's Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work that could change how medicines are made.

item.title: Fuel: government ends duty discount and waits for EU
item.description: The Meloni government has neither renewed the fuel excise discount nor launched the mooted tax rebate scheme. Brussels awaits the 15-16 October European Council, while EU capitals move ahead in a haphazard fashion.

item.title: EU to put energy security at heart of COP31 push for faster green transition
item.description: EU ministers are set to confirm their commitment to the green transition despite soaring energy prices and supply concerns, according to a draft COP31 position seen by Euronews.

item.title: İzmir's centre-left mayor joins Erdoğan's AK Party, shocking Turkish opposition
item.description: Cemil Tugay, who won İzmir for the CHP with a 314,000-vote margin in 2024, received his AK Party badge from Erdoğan in Ankara on Wednesday, ending 27 years of centre-left rule in Turkey's third-largest city.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 7th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 7th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Emirates launches Helsinki flights as airline reaches 93% of pre-disruption capacity
item.description: The Dubai-based airline has touched down in Finland’s capital Helsinki for the first time as it reports operating at around 93% of its pre-disruption capacity.

item.title: Why are Melania Trump staffers gloating about ‘Digger’ and its box office woes?
item.description: A senior advisor to Melania Trump posted a comparison online that doesn't make much sense...

item.title: Hardline Iranian MPs move to impeach foreign minister over UN General Assembly talks
item.description: The motion, filed by MPs aligned with the Paydari Front, accuses Araghchi of meeting US envoy Steve Witkoff at the UN General Assembly without authorisation, a claim directly opposed by Supreme National Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei, who said the talks had prior approval.

item.title: Zelenskyy says Russia missile attack that killed 12 is birthday 'gift' to Putin
item.description: The Ukraine president said energy infrastructure was a key target and renewed his appeal for air defences, as Kyiv residents spent the night sheltering in subway stations.

item.title: EU trade chief heads to Beijing under pressure to deliver on Chinese imports
item.description: Brussels has yet to find a way to curb Chinese imports, while EU leaders demand results from Beijing talks as a trade war looms.

item.title: Russia asks Vietnam for planes as illegally re-registered Western fleet falls apart
item.description: Moscow proposed wet-leasing Vietnamese aircraft, crews and maintenance, but any transfer would involve Airbus or Boeing jets, exposing Vietnamese carriers to secondary sanctions. Nearly a fifth of Russia's largest airlines' planes are already grounded, double the normal downtime rate.

item.title: Czechia withdraws from Eurovision Song Contest 2027 citing budget pressures
item.description: Czech Television said in a statement: "We won't see the Czech flag on stage next year,” citing ongoing financial pressures.

item.title: Removing Russian oligarchs from sanctions list sets 'a very bad precedent', Browder says
item.description: Bill Browder, once Russia’s largest foreign investor, said sanctions are the “worst thing” that can happen to Russian oligarchs, adding that they are “scheming and trying to come up with ways of getting off the sanctions list”.

item.title: IMF chief signals austerity is back as global public debt heads for 100% of GDP
item.description: IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva has urged heavily indebted governments to tighten their belts and central banks to take a hawkish stance, signalling a return to austerity as the energy shock from the Iran war, record public debt and a credit-fuelled AI investment boom weigh on the global economy.

item.title: Balloons, baths and poppy-seed cuisine: discover Afyonkarahisar
item.description: In Afyonkarahisar, hot air balloons drift over 3,000-year-old Phrygian rock carvings, mineral-rich thermal springs have drawn visitors since 1200 BC, and poppy seeds define a UNESCO-recognised culinary tradition.

item.title: Israel pauses in moment of silence to remember those killed on 7 October
item.description: A group representing the bereaved families organised tributes, including a silence at 6:29am - the minute the attack began - and a ceremony that will follow tonight in Tel Aviv.

item.title: Israel's ambassador Zarka: France has a serious antisemitism problem
item.description: The world is marking the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks by Hamas — a day that shocked Israel to its core and reverberated across the region and beyond. Meanwhile, the war against Hamas in Gaza continues to produce a human catastrophe, with tens of thousands dead and no path to peace.

item.title: India hikes interest rates for first time in over three years as Iran war fuels inflation
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India raised borrowing costs for the first time in over three years on Wednesday, as the Middle East war pushes up prices in Asia's third-biggest economy and weighs on an already fragile rupee.

item.title: Eva Marie Saint, ‘North By Northwest’ star and 'On the Waterfront' Oscar winner, dies aged 102
item.description: The Oscar-winning actress was one of the last stars of the Golden Age of Hollywood and was the oldest living Oscar winner.

item.title: Siberia plague outbreak is an 'isolated incident', virologist says
item.description: Belgian virologist Marc Van Ranst says that while people may think of plague as “something medieval”, cases are reported every year in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Madagascar. However, he says the laboratory link makes this incident “a little more serious”.

item.title: Israelis mourn Nova festival victims three years after Hamas attack
item.description: Ceremonies at the Nova festival site and Kfar Aza marked three years since the Hamas-led October 7 attack that sparked the Gaza war.

item.title: Tear gas and fireworks as student protests turn violent in Paris
item.description: Clashes erupt in Paris as school pupils demanding better funding face riot police, amid nationwide protests over shortages and crumbling schools.

item.title: Spat over Israeli flag removal engulfs the European Parliament on October 7 anniversary
item.description: Good morning. It’s Wednesday. On today’s docket: Israel’s Ambassador to France Joshua Zarka responds to mounting controversy over the removal of the Israeli flag at an exhibition in the European Parliament, and the latest on the suspected pneumonic plague outbreak.

item.title: The EU agrees on new Return Order, longer detention and return hubs
item.description: EU ministers agreed on new rules allowing sanctions for migrants who refuse to cooperate with return procedures, detention up to 24 months or longer for security risks, and return hubs outside the EU. Watch the video!

item.title: Christa Pike awake a week after lethal injection as her lawyers seek answers
item.description: Christa Pike remains shackled to her hospital bed with burned and blistered arms, while Tennessee has suspended executions and its prison chief has resigned.

item.title: Invasive plant spreads across Portugal and lengthens allergy season
item.description: Known for its showy plumes and used as an ornamental for decades, pampas grass, also known as Cortaderia selloana, is spreading, threatening biodiversity and raising vegetation management costs. Experts call for urgent action to halt its advance and reduce pollen exposure.

item.title: How Verifactu will affect Spanish SMEs and self-employed after its delay
item.description: The Government's delay in bringing the Verifactu e-invoicing system into force gives firms and the self-employed more time, but fuels uncertainty over its rollout.

item.title: Europe Today: WHO says Siberia plague risk is low as drones sink Black Sea ships
item.description: The WHO says the risk of a plague epidemic is low after a lab worker died in Siberia. We report on the drone attacks that have sunk ships off Romania and Bulgaria in recent days. And: EU envoys are set to approve the biggest Russia sanctions package since 2022.

item.title: 'Potemkin budget’: French government slams Marine Le Pen’s plans
item.description: "You're dreaming in colour", "a Potemkin budget, flimsy as cardboard", "purely incantatory, utterly unenforceable": the government torpedoes the counter-budget put forward by National Rally leader Marine Le Pen.

item.title: UBS only European bank in top 10 of AI adoption as JPMorgan Chase leads
item.description: UBS is now the only European lender among the top 10 banks judged most advanced in adopting artificial intelligence, after HSBC dropped out of the top tier of the Evident AI Index, while JPMorgan Chase widened its lead and North American banks tightened their grip.

item.title: Puigdemont welcomes Spain's amnesty but warns it is not the solution for Catalonia
item.description: The Catalan pro-independence leader, who has lived in self-imposed exile in Waterloo for nine years, hailed the Supreme Court's move to lift his arrest warrant over alleged embezzlement linked to the 'procés'.

item.title: The Caspian Sea has been shrinking for decades. Now, a new island has emerged
item.description: Scientists warn that parts of the northern Caspian could face an Aral Sea-like scenario, while climate change and human water use are adding pressure on the region.

item.title: These are the best wine regions in Europe, with Slovenia claiming top spot above France and Italy
item.description: Štajerska, praised for its authenticity and centuries of wine culture, beat out more than 90 leading territories for the title.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 7th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 7th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Qatar eyes 2036 Olympics after it hosts Asian Games as F1 confirms Gulf races
item.description: Doha will host the Asian Games in 2030 and is among seven potential hosts for the 2036 Olympics, while Formula 1 says its Qatar and Abu Dhabi races will go ahead as scheduled, bringing much-needed relief after months of uncertainty.

item.title: Celebrating the October 7 massacre is inhumanity, not solidarity
item.description: On the anniversary of the Hamas terrorist attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, in which 1,200 people were murdered and 250 were abducted, Sacha Roytman Dratwa, of the ‘Combat Antisemitism Movement’, recalls in an opinion piece for Euronews what had already begun in many countries on 8 October 2023.

item.title: Record bets against the euro: how low could it fall amid France's fiscal crisis and Europe's energy shock?
item.description: The euro hit a 17-month low as French debt fears and Europe's energy shock weigh on the currency. Bond market stress could limit further ECB rate hikes, while analysts see scope for the euro to fall to $1.10 if the pressure intensifies.

item.title: Argentina waves football great Lionel Messi off after 3-0 win over Benin in final international appearance
item.description: All-time footballing icon Lionel Messi bids an emotional farewell to international duty after guiding Argentina to a 3-0 win over visitors Benin in Buenos Aires. The little magician produced a final breathtaking performance for his white and blue stripes, scoring one goal and assisting two others.

item.title: Former German foreign intelligence chief August Hanning arrested on suspicion of espionage, attempted treason
item.description: August Hanning is accused of illegally receiving classified information during his time in office and after vacating his post, which were improperly used for his personal consultancy work.

item.title: Sánchez announces 21 urgent housing measures after nationwide protests ahead of snap election
item.description: Sánchez has come under fire domestically after an 87-year-old woman was evicted from her residence in Madrid, sparking national controversy. Pressure have piled on Sanchez’s administration to step down as protesters accused the government of not doing enough to tackle a rampant housing crisis.

item.title: Armed Man shot outside Sweden's Royal Palace in Stockholm
item.description: Swedish police have shot and wounded an armed man outside the royal palace in central Stockholm. The man has been taken to a hospital.

item.title: Judo: Japan crowns two new world champions in Baku
item.description: Akari Omori claimed her first world title at -57kg, defeating reigning champion Eteri Liparteliani in golden score. At -73kg, Ryuga Tanaka overcame Makhmadbek Makhmadbekov in a tight final to secure gold and complete a double triumph for Japan.

item.title: UK trial of three Iranians over alleged plot to target Iran dissident journalists
item.description: In London three Iranians go on trial accused of targeting UK-based journalists opposed to the regime in Tehran

item.title: Swedish Patriot missiles to be sent to Poland to bolster NATO's eastern flank
item.description: Sweden will send Patriot air-defences and around 100 troops to protect the Rzeszów-Jasionka logistics hub used to route aid to Ukraine. The mission starts on 1 December and will last seven months.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 6th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 6th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: One student killed, eight wounded in Istanbul school stabbing attack
item.description: A 15-year-old student disguised herself in the target school's uniform before attacking pupils at Şeyh Şamil Imam Hatip Secondary School in Başakşehir on Tuesday morning. The suspect, who attends a different school, was apprehended.

item.title: A heavy lift: Thieves steal Dalí's 200kg diamond-studded 'Book of the Apocalypse' in France
item.description: Police in central France are searching for an art collector's book worth an estimated €1 million that was stolen from an art centre in Issoire in Puy‑de‑Dôme. The "Book of the Apocalypse", a 210‑kilo volume contains works by Salvador Dalí, Jean Cocteau and Bernard Buffet.
